facts.fact: Per Leichtman Research Group data, approximately 34.4% of U.S. households still subscribe to traditional pay-TV (cable, satellite, or telco TV) as of late 2025.
facts.quote: Per Leichtman Research Group data from late 2025, approximately 34.4% of U.S. households still subscribe to traditional pay-TV (cable, satellite, or telco TV).

facts.fact: Approximately 66% of U.S. households do not have pay-TV, a figure that includes both cord cutters and cord nevers.
facts.quote: Approximately 66% (includes both "cord cutters" who previously subscribed and "cord nevers" who never did)

facts.fact: The page reports that the U.S. pay-TV industry lost 5 million subscribers in 2025.
Per company reporting, Comcast lost approximately 1.15 million pay-TV video subscribers in 2025, including 245,000 in Q4 2025 alone.
facts.quote: Approximately 1.15 million video subscribers (245,000 in Q4 2025 alone), per company reporting

facts.fact: YouTube TV added approximately 100,000 subscribers in Q1 2025.
facts.quote: YouTube TV:** Added approximately 100,000 subscribers in Q1 2025, the only major pay-TV operator to grow during that period

facts.fact: U.S. pay-TV household penetration peaked at roughly 82-83% in 2011.
facts.quote: Historical peak:** U.S. pay-TV penetration peaked at roughly 82-83% in 2011

facts.fact: Industry coverage in late 2025 indicated annual declines in pay-TV household penetration of closer to 1-2 percentage points, versus steeper drops in 2020-2022.
facts.quote: Industry coverage in late 2025 indicated annual declines closer to 1-2 percentage points in household penetration rather than the steeper drops of 2020-2022.

facts.fact: According to the page, a cable TV ad in 2026 reaches approximately 34% of U.S. households at most.
facts.quote: In 2026, a cable ad reaches approximately 34% of U.S. households at most.

facts.fact: As of the page's writing, Leichtman Research Group had not yet published Q1 2026 data for individual pay-TV providers, so the figures shown reflect the most recent published data.
facts.quote: Q1 2026 data for individual providers was not yet publicly available at the time of this writing

facts.fact: About 34.4% of U.S. households still subscribe to some form of traditional pay-TV, according to the page's Q1 2026 cord-cutting figures.
facts.quote: About 34.4% of households still subscribe to some form of traditional pay-TV.

facts.fact: Approximately 66% of U.S. households no longer subscribe to traditional pay-TV, based on Leichtman Research Group data from late 2025 (this figure includes cord cutters and cord nevers).
facts.quote: Approximately 66% of U.S. households no longer subscribe to traditional pay-TV, based on Leichtman Research Group data from late 2025.

facts.fact: Industry coverage in late 2025 indicated annual declines in pay-TV penetration of roughly 1-2 percentage points, down from steeper drops during 2020-2022.
facts.quote: Industry coverage in late 2025 indicated annual declines of roughly 1-2 percentage points, down from steeper drops during 2020-2022.

facts.fact: YouTube TV added approximately 100,000 subscribers in Q1 2025 while traditional pay-TV operators lost subscribers.
